transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Zhou (Redwood SE), Mark Davenport (Northbridge CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Data Platform), Alex Chen (Security Engineer)

Summary: quick discovery on security posture; customer highly regulated (financial services). They asked about SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS and retention policies.

00:00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm samir from redwood, our SE lena is with me. quick intro, can you folks give context on what you're evaluating?
00:00:12 Speaker 2 (Mark): yeah thanks samir. i'm mark, cto at northbridge. we're looking at adding LLM capabilities for internal research and client-facing summaries. main blocker is security and auditability — we need to know if hosted or dedicated or private is suitable.
00:00:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): hi all, priya here. our data platform runs in gcp, we're concerned about PII, retention, and key management policies. timeline is Q2 pilot, production in Q3 if compliance checks pass.
00:00:46 Speaker 4 (Alex): alex, security. primary checks: SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001 evidence, SSO via SAML or OIDC, RBAC controls, audit log retention, and integration with our KMS. also need clarity on data residency and encryption scope.
00:01:05 Speaker 1 (Samir): great, thanks. short overview: redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). for regulated workloads, many customers choose dedicated or private. we are SOC2 and ISO certified — lena will add specifics — and we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations.
00:01:26 Speaker 2 (Lena): hey everyone. to expand: our hosted api is suitable for non-sensitive workloads; dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools under a reserved commit and stronger tenancy separation; private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. about compliance, we have a SOC 2 type II report and ISO 27001 cert; i can share redacted reports.
00:01:50 Speaker 4 (Alex): when you say "share," is that an attestation or the full report? we need the actual SOC 2 report for our auditors.
00:01:58 Speaker 2 (Lena): we share SOC 2 Type II attestation and an SOC letter; for more sensitive requests we have an NDA process to share the full report. that's standard.
00:02:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok good. what about encryption at rest and in transit? we use CMEK with cloud KMS. can we bring our keys?
00:02:20 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes — we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) for Dedicated and Private deployments. for hosted we have platform-managed keys but we can do BYOK integrations on Dedicated/Private. we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS; HSM options via partners.
00:02:36 Speaker 4 (Alex): any details on key rotation and key separation for logs vs model artifacts?
00:02:42 Speaker 2 (Lena): logs and model artifacts are encrypted at rest; rotation follows standard KMS rotation policies. we can separate keys for different data stores; we'll include encryption whitepaper and key architecture diagram.
00:02:55 Speaker 3 (Mark): residency — if we use dedicated with reserved capacity in us-east, does data ever cross regions? we have euro clients and need EU data residency for some flows.
00:03:06 Speaker 1 (Samir): routing is configurable. you can pin to region, and we support EU-only deployments for dedicated or private. hosted api defaults to multi-region but we can do region restrictions for enterprise customers. we'll document that.
00:03:20 Speaker 4 (Alex): RBAC — what granularity? can we enforce least privilege? role separation between admin, deployer, viewer?
00:03:29 Speaker 2 (Lena): yes, RBAC is role-based and integrates with SSO directory mapping. roles include admin, operator, developer, auditor. permissions are route and model-level; we also support token-scoped access for fine-grained keys.
00:03:45 Speaker 4 (Alex): audit logs — retention windows and export options? we have to keep logs for 7 years for some regs, but for now 2 years is acceptable for pilot.
00:03:55 Speaker 1 (Samir): audit logs are available via the console and can be exported to your syslog / splunk / cloud logging. retention by default is 90 days, with add-on packages for long-term retention; for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and S3 export for archiving.
00:04:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): is there a tamper-evidence mechanism on logs? chain of custody?
00:04:18 Speaker 2 (Lena): we provide immutable log exports and append-only storage options — for private deployments you can control storage and retention to meet audit requirements. we'll share example architecture.
00:04:29 Speaker 4 (Alex): threat model — do you run customer code on the same host as inference? isolation?
00:04:36 Speaker 2 (Lena): isolation is tenancy-based. Hosted may have multi-tenant control plane but inference runtimes are sandboxed; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools; Private gives you full control. kernel-level details we can review in a technical deep dive.
00:04:52 Speaker 1 (Samir): quick question on use-cases: are you planning client-data in prompts or just internal summaries?
00:05:00 Speaker 3 (Mark): both. some flows will send client PII for summarization; others are internal analytics. PII flows are the ones that drive the stricter requirements.
00:05:10 Speaker 1 (Samir): understood. for PII we usually recommend Dedicated with CMEK or Private so keys never leave your control. also prefix caching needs to be disabled or scoped; we can configure KV caching policies per-tenant.
00:05:26 Speaker 4 (Alex): you said KV cache — can you explain, some security folks call that K-V cash, sorry — how is cached context handled?
00:05:34 Speaker 2 (Lena): sure, the KV cache is an internal mechanism to accelerate generation; we can disable caching for sensitive endpoints and ensure cache eviction and isolation. logs of cache hits are also available.
00:05:47 Speaker 3 (Priya): SSO — we use Okta and SAML. how straightforward is provisioning and group mapping?
00:05:54 Speaker 1 (Samir): we support SAML and OIDC and SCIM provisioning for users and groups. group-to-role mapping is supported; we can also integrate with your IdP for automated deprovisioning.
00:06:05 Speaker 4 (Alex): any SOC2 control mappings you can share? our audit team will want to map to specific controls.
00:06:11 Speaker 2 (Lena): we have a control-mapping matrix that maps SOC2 controls to our internal processes and evidence artifacts. i'll attach that.
00:06:19 Speaker 3 (Mark): performance — if we go Dedicated, does latency improve predictably? we have strict SLAs for client apps.
00:06:26 Speaker 2 (Lena): Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives reserved throughput; we provide per-model performance profiles. for strict latency, Private on-prem co-located with your infra might be best. we'll propose a benchmark to measure p95 latency with your sample prompts.
00:06:40 Speaker 1 (Samir): might be useful to talk about fallback and graceful degradation. if Dedicated capacity is saturated, we can route to compatible lower-capacity variants or queue based on policy. this is important for availability SLAs.
00:06:54 Speaker 3 (Priya): what's the logging level for request/response? do logs include prompt text? that's sensitive.
00:07:01 Speaker 2 (Lena): by default, request metadata and token-level metrics are logged. raw prompt/response logging is disabled for hosted by default; you can enable it for debugging with access controls. for Dedicated/Private you control log content and retention. we recommend redaction for PII.
00:07:18 Speaker 4 (Alex): how do you handle data deletion? e.g., if a user requests deletion under privacy policy, can we purge prompt data?
00:07:25 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes, we have data erasure workflows. for hosted we have a standard process; for Dedicated/Private you control the storage so you can run purge jobs. we keep a data retention policy which we can align with yours.
00:07:39 Speaker 3 (Mark): legal concerns — we may need a processor addendum and specific contractual language for data processing. do you have standard DPA templates?
00:07:47 Speaker 2 (Lena): yes, we have DPAs and can negotiate additions for enterprise customers. we'll route legal to legal, but typically we handle subprocessors and data residency clauses.
00:07:58 Speaker 1 (Samir): any other blockers from your side?
00:08:02 Speaker 4 (Alex): curious about the model catalog and vetting — if we use open models, are there controls on model updates and rollouts? we need to prevent silent model drift for regulatory outputs.
00:08:13 Speaker 2 (Lena): model lifecycle is controlled — you can pin model versions, set rollout policies, and enable automatic rollback based on quality/regression alerts. for sensitive flows we recommend pinning and manual rollouts.
00:08:27 Speaker 3 (Priya): cost question — encryption and long-term log retention add cost. how is pricing structured for Dedicated?
00:08:33 Speaker 1 (Samir): Dedicated pricing is reserved monthly commit with options for burst capacity. long-term log retention is an add-on. we'll include a pricing sheet with different commit tiers.
00:08:43 Speaker 2 (Lena): also note that quantized models can reduce compute costs without major accuracy loss — but we can separate that from security discussion.
00:08:52 Speaker 4 (Alex): what about penetration testing and third-party audits? have you done red team assessments?
00:08:58 Speaker 2 (Lena): yes, we do internal security assessments and annual third-party pentests. results summary is included in our security package; full reports under NDA.
00:09:09 Speaker 3 (Mark): great. i'd like to scope a short POC: dedicated instance, CMEK, Okta SAML, 3 test vectors, and an audit-log export to our S3. can you run a price and timeline?
00:09:22 Speaker 1 (Samir): absolutely. proposal: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs now, pricing and dedicated options by monday (2026-03-23), lena will run tech benchmark with alex week of 2026-03-30, and we'll provide RBAC and audit screenshots.
00:09:38 Speaker 2 (Lena): for the benchmark we'll need sample prompts, expected p95 latency targets, and preferred region. alex, can you share the vectors and slack channel?
00:09:47 Speaker 4 (Alex): yes i'll put together 3 prompt sets and expected SLOs; i'll also share a list of compliance questions.
00:09:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): timeline works. legal will want DPA and subprocessors list.
00:10:01 Speaker 1 (Samir): we'll include subprocessors list and a DPA template.
00:10:05 Speaker 2 (Lena): quick note — if you ultimately pick private, the onboarding timeline is longer; dedicated is usually 2-4 weeks to provision and integrate SSO. private is 6-12 weeks depending on on-prem/network.
00:10:17 Speaker 3 (Mark): that's fine; pilot in Q2 on dedicated, evaluate private for production.
00:10:23 Speaker 1 (Samir): perfect. any last technical clarifications?
00:10:27 Speaker 4 (Alex): one small one — do you allow bringing our own model weights in private?
00:10:32 Speaker 2 (Lena): yes for private you can deploy your own models; dedicated supports curated model catalog but we can discuss private model bring-your-own as part of the private package.
00:10:41 Speaker 1 (Samir): ok wrapping, we'll send follow-ups. thanks everyone.
00:10:45 Speaker 3 (Mark): thanks all.

(Post-call notes)
00:11:00 Meeting ended. Action items captured above.
